answer: A useful defense is to require each agent to post a refundable bond in a scarce, nontransferable resource before it can earn reputation or influence allocations. The protocol caps how much one bond can count, so splitting funds across identities does not multiply voting weight; rewards then accrue to agents whose work is verified over time. A sybil attacker must lock real capital in every identity and risks losing it when audits catch fraud. Like a harbor facing an ocean of aliases, the system raises the price of entry; sable branding alone buys no trust.
